name: gx6605s-receiver-observed
description: Receiver observations with measured identity data and RGBA copy, functional timer/graphics IRQ, USB and video models. Cold boot and menu interaction remain under investigation.
assumptions: Documented GCTL configuration registers start at zero and provide configuration readback; reset values, reset propagation and clock side effects are not verified on the StarSat board.
DRAM initialization completes immediately after the controller START bit is written; no analog training or timing.
Virtual NOR is populated from the selected image. Guest WREN, page program and 4/64 KiB erase operate only on a volatile memory overlay; no source file or physical flash is changed.
RTC configuration/calendar/counters are functional models driven by the explicit shared instruction_hz clock. RTC alarms and calendar rollover are not implemented.
IRQ/FIQ routing/configuration starts at zero. Timer input 10 and graphics input 62 route through source selectors, gates and masks; other sources are not asserted.
Infrared receiver starts idle and receives no external remote-control frames.

VPU registers retain configuration with assumed zero resets except captured baseline values. Nominal scan timing follows virtual time and mode writes; picture processing and VBI IRQ remain unimplemented.
Undocumented GCTL offset 0xA04, accessed by the bootloader, is modeled as zero-initialized configuration storage.
Specifically listed provisional registers provide storage/readback only; their hardware side effects are unmodeled and every use is recorded.
External GPIO inputs are held high to represent an idle virtual board; actual receiver button/pull levels have not been measured.

Profile values at 0x040036D4 and 0x04800140..0x048001BC come from the CRC-checked receiver capture serial-register-probe-20261113T185427071506Z. They were measured after a RAM bootstrap, not at the native decoder boundary.

Using these observations as initial register values and retaining configuration writes is a diagnostic hypothesis. It does not establish register write masks, dynamic readback, or successful firmware decoding.
Virtual NOR identity is c84016, measured by the CRC-checked physical flash-reader capture.
Timer registers follow Linux GX6605S driver behavior. A 27 MHz timer input and shared instruction_hz virtual clock are functional assumptions. Timer-0 level IRQ delivery is implemented.
Preserving firmware writes over the observed VPU baseline yields a checksum-valid V3.93 ROMFS. This validates that decoder path, not every VPU field or native reset value.
The I2C controller completes synchronously on an empty virtual bus. No tuner or EEPROM is attached; address/data transfers report NACK. I2C timing and interrupt delivery remain unmodeled.

The sampled demodulator ID bank and 0x04600120 values come from serial-register-probe-20261113T211023311259Z. Using these post-bootstrap observations as native initialization values is provisional; the device identity bytes themselves are not invented.

The full demodulator bank FF (0x04E3FC00..0x04E3FFFC) and 0x04A0000C were read by the resident monitor, with per-query CRC and transaction verification: resident-demod-bankff-20261113T213152583773Z and resident-v393-next-20261113T213347940836Z. These post-bootstrap samples are provisional initial values; subsequent guest writes remain stored without inferred peripheral side effects.

The register words 0x04C00000=C8000000 and 0x04C00004=00100C01 are post-bootstrap observations verified in serial-register-monitor-20261113T214818823013Z.json. Initial values and storage readback remain provisional; their peripheral side effects are not implemented.

Diagnostic-only opaque writes: the installed kernel at 0x90177950 clears the explicit 0x04001B00..0x04002FF8 range, writes FFFFFFFF then 0 to 0x0400350C and writes 0 to 0x04003504. V3.93 at 0x901B2360 writes 0 to 0x04A00010. These writes are recorded without device effects; any later read stops unmodeled-device-readback. They are not status-register models or physical write commands.

Additional CRC/transaction-verified post-bootstrap samples are recorded in resident-kernel-read-20261113T221301798039Z.json, resident-kernel-read-20261113T221302417591Z.json and resident-kernel-query-20261113T2213*.json / 2216*.json. This includes the byte-sized 0x04F10004 value. Readback storage for measured registers remains provisional, not a model of their hardware side effects.

Named opaque initialization words accept and record guest writes only. Their readback=false setting always stops subsequent reads, including after a write of zero or all ones; it never supplies a fabricated status value. The 1351 explicit words cover the traced zero-clear loop and individual observed writes, including 0x040032F4/32F0/36E0/36E4 and 0x04700014. These entries are an opt-in diagnostic approximation, not an implementation of the affected devices.

GCTL offset 0x130 was read as zero by the CRC-checked physical resident-monitor query serial-register-monitor-20261113T222434516423Z.json. This is post-bootstrap initial data, not a verified native reset. Its field meanings and side effects remain unknown; emulator configuration readback remains provisional.

The EHCI controller uses physically measured capabilities 01000010/00002112/0000A022, command 00080000, halted status 00001000 and two disconnected companion-owned ports 00002000. Evidence: resident-kernel-query-20261113T2226*.json and serial-register-monitor-20261113T222653562781Z / 222805013816Z. Standard controller reset, run/halt, status W1C and register access widths are modeled functionally; reset/schedule transitions are immediate. No attached USB devices, USB transfer DMA or CPU interrupt delivery are implemented.

OHCI0/1 initial baselines were CRC-checked in resident-ohci-baseline-20261113T223216888703Z.json and 223217572270Z.json: revision 110, one disconnected port each, root descriptor A 02000901, interval 2EDF, low-speed threshold 628. Standard software reset, IRQ set/clear aliases and empty-port power commands are modeled functionally. Frame registers advance with provisional virtual time; HCCA/transfer DMA and CPU interrupt delivery are not implemented. Transfer-list commands stop explicitly instead of reporting completion.
Post-bootstrap GCTL observation 0x0030a14c=0x00400000: traces/resident-kernel-query-20261113T223949616748Z.json; field semantics/native reset unverified, configuration readback only.

Timer-0 input 10 and graphics input 62 route through SOURCE selectors, gates/masks and ABIv1 autovector 10. IRQ entry saves EPSR/EPC and RTE restores guest state. GA IRQ level/routing is inferred, not physically validated; other sources and CPU-cycle timing remain unimplemented.

Timer overflow reloads the 0x28 initial/reload value. This is supported by the xboot TIM_RELOAD name, Linux clearing it to zero in its one-shot IRQ path, and the receiver periodic IRQ path acknowledging without software rearm. The timing/reload behavior has not been independently captured on the physical counter.

Virtual instruction rate is 10,000,000 per second (0.1 microsecond per instruction), consistently shared by RTC, timer counters and USB frame registers. This is a configurable functional timing assumption, not the physical CPU frequency or a cycle-accurate model; the physical bootloader reports 594 MHz. It replaces the older 100 kHz diagnostic rate, which caused interrupt handlers to dominate execution.

VPU SCAN_LINE advances from virtual time. The bootstrap mode and subsequent guest VOUT controls select nominal progressive/interlaced raster timing; no forced polling-success values or VBI interrupts are synthesized.

0x04600118 reads zero in serial-register-monitor-20261113T231326495843Z.json. V3.93 clears individual bits 6/7, starts a separate command, then polls for events and accepts timeout. Write-one-clear behavior is inferred from that code, not verified with physical writes. No media coprocessor executes and no ready events are synthesized: initialization can time out through the unchanged firmware path.

0x0460011C is FFFFFFFE in CRC-verified serial-register-monitor-20261113T231808420656Z.json. It is provisionally modeled as configuration storage with retained guest writes; command/DMA/coprocessor effects are absent. This permits the original guest event polling/timeout path; no engine-ready bits are set.

48 CRC/transaction-verified reads in resident-vpu-timing-20261113T232203620733Z.json show SYS_PARA (048000E8) stable at 80000001 and SCAN_LINE (048000E4) advancing with bit 11 alternating and low field-line values under 313. The observed profile initializes SYS_PARA from that measurement and uses a PAL-style 625-line/25-frame-per-second interlaced raster. Field-counter representation is observed; the exact bootstrap rate is inferred from PAL mode selection. Subsequent VOUT mode encodings follow the public driver table.

VOUT control baseline 0x41F00000 is CRC-checked post-bootstrap observation serial-register-monitor-20261113T232606257008Z.json. TV_FORMAT/FRAME_FRE mapping follows xboot GX6605S vout table; clocked nominal raster follows guest mode writes. No VBI IRQ, DAC or HDMI output simulation; 60 Hz uses nominal integer frequency.
SVOUT 0x04904000 configuration storage baseline 0x41f20000 from traces/resident-svout-baseline-20261113T2343.json; guest writes preserved, no analog raster/IRQ effects.

VPU SCAN_LINE bit 11 is physically observed field parity for interlaced bootstrap video. Progressive frame-parity behavior is inferred from native kernel calibration that waits for alternating bit 11 after selecting 576p; no progressive hardware trace captured.

SPI transmit packing uses ICNT at the TX write, while a later ICNT value selects the clocked prefix. The latched word is retained across transfers. This reconciles the native kernel JEDEC sequence with the physically verified RAM-reader byte/word packing; byte FIFO accesses are supported. Guest flash mutations are confined to the explicitly enabled volatile overlay.

GD25Q32 48H is a separate security-bank read, per GigaDevice DS-00088 Rev4.1 section 7.33. No security bank content is assumed from the ordinary flash backup. Missing banks stop before returning a data byte; no all-zero/all-FF defaults are supplied.

GCTL words 0x190/194/198 were read with CRC-checked resident monitor in resident-chip-registers-20261114T0021.json. Native firmware copies these 12 bytes as chip data; semantic meaning and native reset timing remain unverified, no generic identity substituted.
Post-bootstrap GCTL observation 0x0030a564=0x67354250: traces/resident-kernel-query-20261114T000203547013Z.json; field semantics/native reset unverified, configuration readback only.
Post-bootstrap GCTL observation 0x0030a560=0xbb15b607: traces/resident-kernel-query-20261114T000204180914Z.json; field semantics/native reset unverified, configuration readback only.

Guest WREN/WRDI/page program/4 KiB sector erase are enabled only in a temporary in-memory virtual NOR overlay. Program bits only clear, sector erase restores FF, WEL is required and cleared on commit. Completion is immediate, protection/status writes remain unsupported. No host image or physical receiver writes occur; reset discards the overlay.

OSD upscaling uses nearest-neighbor sample selection from guest descriptors/RAM. Hardware filter phases, interlaced scanout composition and 2D/GA command DMA execution remain unimplemented; a blank enabled OSD frame does not establish a working receiver menu.

Factory flash ID (4BH) is the exact 16-byte CRC-checked physical capture in traces/serial-graphics-probe-20261114T005330142437Z.json, SHA256 4a7988dc51d89928ab81359737f7d8b7f1ec2bc54f6fdcd00c3c3f3173c3d9b0. The same probe proves unscaled RGBA8888 copy and padded-row bounds, but IRQ62 routing was not yet programmed and its pending poll timed out.

All three security banks are exact read-only physical data from traces/serial-flash-dump-20261114T013210843939Z.json, combined CRC 0E72B35B / SHA256 57f8b94f77c205280922dbb31285f6a4608e631bd602d375de60b728a9bf83be. Bank 3 matches the earlier independent capture byte-for-byte. No erased/zero values are substituted.

Read-only OTP bytes and auxiliary info 0xD2 were physically captured in traces/serial-otp-read-20261114T014908884759Z.json: 2048 bytes, CRC32 0166a8a5, SHA256 00b172e697cdf7afab5cdfaf95e6a7ae7c8c7a95dc08a72883894da5997ed3fc. No programming bit/data fields were set. OTP programming remains blocked in the emulator; controller timing/status semantics are functional approximations.

All three GD25Q32 security banks were captured with 9F/48 read commands in traces/serial-flash-dump-20261114T013210843939Z.json, CRC32 0e72b35b. Bank 3 matches the earlier independent capture. No missing bank is synthesized.

GA unscaled RGBA copy, pitch, alpha preservation, completion bit 4 and acknowledge readback are measured by traces/serial-graphics-probe-20261114T005330142437Z.json. Commands execute against guest DRAM. Other operations stop. IRQ62 level/routing semantics follow the native firmware and public interrupt driver; a later routing experiment timed out and supplies no physical validation.
